6                 IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                    
7                     FOR THE DISTRICT OF ARIZONA                        
8                                                                        
9   BBK Tobacco & Foods LLP,           No. CV-19-05216-PHX-MTL           
10              Plaintiff,              ORDER                             
11   v.                                                                   
12   Central Coast Agriculture Incorporated,                              
13              Defendant.                                                
14                                                                        
15        Before the Court is Defendant Central Coast Agriculture, Inc.’s (“CCA”) Motion to 
16   Strike Jury Demand (the “Motion”). (Doc. 558.)                       
17                                 I.                                     
18        The relevant factual background and procedural history have been thoroughly 
19   addressed in prior orders, including the Order regarding summary judgment. (See Doc. 
20   443.) As such, the Court only briefly restates the facts relevant to deciding the pending 
21   Motion.                                                              
22        Plaintiff BBK Tobacco & Foods LLP’s (“BBK”) Amended Complaint seeks relief 
23   for trademark infringement and unfair competition under federal and Arizona law. (Doc. 
24   60.)  BBK seeks  disgorgement of profits, injunctive relief, and corrective  advertising 
25   damages on these claims. (Id.; Doc. 558-1 at 4-7.) BBK demands a jury trial in its 
26   Complaint. (Doc. 60.)                                                
27        Fact discovery closed on May 14, 2021. (Doc. 31 at 2.) Dispositive motions were 
28   due by January 14, 2022. (Id. at 5.) CCA previously filed two motions for partial summary 
1   judgment with leave from the Court for the second. (Docs. 182, 203.) 
2        On August 6, 2024, the Ninth Circuit reversed the Court’s summary judgment on 
3   Counts I-V. (Doc. 466-1 at 6.) The Court  then reopened  summary judgment on the 
4   remaining claims. (Doc. 470.) CCA subsequently filed its third motion for summary 
5   judgment (Doc. 485), which the Court granted in part and denied in part on February 28, 
6   2025 (Doc. 556).                                                     
7        CCA now files the present Motion to strike BBK’s jury demand on the basis that 
8   BBK has not presented sufficient evidence regarding its harm.        
9                                 II.                                    
10        The Seventh Amendment provides that, “In Suits at common law, where the value 
11   in controversy shall exceed twenty dollars, the right of trial by jury shall be preserved . . . .” 
12   U.S. Const. amend. VII. “The Seventh Amendment guarantees a litigant’s right to a jury 
13   trial on ‘suits at common law.’” Fifty-Six Hope Rd. Music, Ltd. v. A.V.E.L.A., Inc., 778 
14   F.3d 1059, 1074 (9th Cir. 2015) (citing U.S. Const. amend. VII). “‘Suits at common law’ 
15   include statutory claims that are legal (as opposed to equitable).” Id. at 1075 (citing Feltner 
16   v. Columbia Pictures Television, Inc., 523 U.S. 340, 348 (1998)). “[A]wards of actual 
17   damages . . . generally are thought to constitute legal relief.” Feltner, 523 U.S. at 346 (citing 
18   Dairy Queen, Inc. v. Wood, 369 U.S. 469, 477 (1962)).                
19                                 III.                                   
20        The Parties agree that BBK has no right to a jury trial on the equitable remedies it 
21   seeks. (Doc 558 at 2.) The Parties dispute whether BBK is entitled to a jury trial based on 
22   its claims for corrective advertising damages. (See Docs. 558 at 3, 559 at 3.) This Order 
23   focuses on BBK’s right to a jury trial on its corrective advertising claims. 
24        CCA argues that none of the remaining claims are triable to a jury based on a lack 
25   of evidence and thus, BBK’s jury demand should be stricken. (Doc. 558 at 2-3.) BBK 
26   argues that “CCA’s Motion is merely a motion for partial summary judgment.” (Doc. 559 
27   at 5.)                                                               
28                                                                        
1        The  Court  agrees  that  CCA’s  Motion  is,  in  essence,  a  motion  for  summary 
2   judgment. CCA argues that BBK “cannot produce evidence to support its jury demand.” 
3   (Doc. 558 at 7.) CCA maintains that BBK cannot show a genuine issue of fact for trial 
4   regarding BBK’s harm. (Id. at 2.) CCA admits that the analysis it seeks is evaluated under 
5   the Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 56, the same standard as a motion for summary 
6   judgment. (Id. at 7.); see Mittelstadt v. Summit Cnty. Legal Aid Soc., 825 F.2d 411, at *3 
7   (6th Cir. 1987) (unpublished table decision) (“The substance of the damage claims [in a 
8   motion to strike a jury demand] are tested under the same standards as those applicable to 
9   a motion for summary judgment under Fed. R. Civ. P. 56.”).           
10        The deadline to file dispositive motions was on January 14, 2022. (Doc. 31 at 5.) 
11   The Scheduling Order states that each Party is permitted only one motion for summary 
12   judgment under Rule 56 without leave from the Court. (Id.) While the Parties stipulated to 
13   the filing of this Motion (See Doc. 546), neither the Parties nor the Court agreed to what is 
14   essentially another motion for summary judgment. As BBK noted, it was unaware that the 
15   Motion would raise an “absence of proof” issue. (Doc. 559 at 6 n.5.)  
16        CCA’s Motion is not a typical motion to strike the jury demand; it asks the Court to 
17   address substantive legal and evidentiary issues appropriate for a motion for summary 
18   judgment. Yet CCA  did not raise these  issues in its previous  motions for summary 
19   judgment when it had the opportunity to do so.                       
20        BBK offers several pieces of evidence which concern harm to BBK because of the 
21   alleged trademark infringement. BBK presents advertising expenditures evidencing the 
22   goodwill of the RAW marks (Doc. 559 at 12), testimony (Doc. 559-4 at 3-4) and email 
23   correspondence  (Doc.  559-2  at  2)  from  Joshua  Kesselman  pertaining  to  consumer 
24   confusion, testimony from Matthew Colvard (Doc. 558-3 at 7) concerning “potential” 
25   harm,  and  an  expert  report  regarding  consumer  confusion  from  Dr.  Jeffrey  Stec 
26   (Doc. 314-1 at 6-7).                                                 
27        The Court abstains from addressing whether this evidence is sufficient to warrant 
28   relief at this stage. See Forest Hills Early Learning Ctr., Inc. v. Lukhard, 728 F.2d 230, 
        233,  245  (4th  Cir.  1984)  (upholding  denial  of  summary  judgment  because  although 
  ||  summary judgment  could have  been  granted,  there  were  “critical  inadequacies  in  the 
      record”); Flores v. Kelley, 61 F.R.D. 442, 445-47 (N.D. Ind.  1973) (exercising discretion 
4||    to deny partial summary judgment where some issues were technically ripe for summary 
5 ||  disposition but intertwined with issues not proper for summary adjudication). 
6          BBK timely demanded a jury trial. (See Doc. 60); Fed. R. Civ. P. 38(b)(1). BBK 
7\|    seeks corrective advertising costs, which are a form of actual damages. Adray v. Adry- 
  ||  Mart,  Inc.,  76  F.3d  984,  988  (9th  Cir.  1995)  (“An  award  of the  cost  of corrective 
9||    advertising, like compensatory damage awards in general, is intended to make the plaintiff 
10 ||  whole. It does so by allowing the plaintiff to recover the cost of advertising undertaken to 
11 |}  restore the  value plaintiff’s  trademark has  lost due  to  defendant’s  infringement.”).  An 
12 ||  award of actual damages is generally considered legal relief. Feltner, 523 U.S. at 346. The 
13 ||  Seventh Amendment protects the right to a jury for this legal claim. Fifty-Six Hope Rd. 
       Music, 778 F.3d at 1074. 
15                                        IV. 
16          Accordingly, 
17          IT IS ORDERED denying CCA’s Motion. (Doc. 558.) 
18          Dated this 30th day of May, 2025. 
19 
°                                     WMichak  T.  Shure 
71                                                  Michael T. Liburdi 
22                                             United  States District Judge 
23
